reports.title: Winston Harris
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The care plan for Mr Harris did not deal with his risk of absconding. As a result when he was transferred to City Hospital with his care plan there were no details of his previous absconding behaviour.
When Mr Harris was transferred to hospital, without an escort, there was no written documentation provided to confirm that a DOLS had been applied for and that he was an absconding risk.

At no time did staff consider if Mr Harris should be subject to an emergency DOLS despite him having dementia and having tried to leave the ward on 16/03/2016. He had previously been assessed as requiring and DOLS.

The application for DOLS order was not processed before Mr [name redacted] death. | heard evidence that it often takes many months to process a DOLS application. Given these are extremely vulnerable people applications should be processed more quickly.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight failures in the timely assessment or processing of deprivation of liberty safeguarding (DOLS) orders, leaving residents without proper legal authority to be detained. The earlier report notes a missing system for reassessment when orders expire, while the later report points to delayed processing of a DOLS application before a resident's death.
